questions.stem: Thornbury Electronics, a fast-growing firm began a quarter with 2,589 subscribers in Kingsford and lost 642 of them during the quarter. What was the churn rate, to one decimal?
questions.explanation: Churn rate is customers lost divided by customers at the start, times 100. With 642 lost from 2,589, that is about 24.8 percent. The complement, about 75.2 percent, is the retention rate, which is a different measure. Inverting the ratio is meaningless. Reducing churn is often cheaper than acquiring new customers.
questions.hint: Divide customers lost by the starting customer count.

inverts lost and starting subscribers
rounds away the decimal

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Eastbrook Confectionery, a mid-sized firm estimates that a Ironvale customer generates $97 in annual contribution margin and that the annual retention rate is 80 percent. Using a simple perpetuity approximation, what is the customer lifetime value?
questions.explanation: In a simple retention-based lifetime value model, CLV equals annual contribution margin divided by the churn rate, where churn is one minus the retention rate. With churn of 20 percent, that is $97 divided by 0.20, giving about $485. Multiplying by a fixed number of years ignores that customers can leave at any time, and multiplying by churn is the wrong direction.
questions.hint: Divide annual margin by one minus the retention rate.
questions.learningObjective: compute a simple customer lifetime value

options.misconception: multiplies by churn instead of dividing by it
divides by the number of years, which the simple model does not use
ignores retention and just multiplies by a fixed life
